description: Train a sparse autoencoder on the tiny CPU Llama: a 16 -> 32 dictionary for layer 0's output, fitted to every token of the weekday prompts after BOS (`{'index': '1:'}`: position 0 is BOS; a ragged read through `fit.dictionary`, one forward per minibatch of 2 prompts). The objective is the dictionary's own scalars: `reconstruction`, the mean squared error between each read vector and its decoding, plus 0.01 times `l1`, the mean absolute latent. Its decoder rows are kept at unit norm by a projection after each optimizer step. The trained dictionary is saved as a bundle (sae_train_ablation.json loads it) with each scalar's per-epoch history. The model is random, so its latents mean nothing; the mechanics are what this exercises.
